sections.html:
Mahaska County is a south-central Iowa county where 22,190 people lived in 2020. Oskaloosa is the county seat and by far the largest city at 11,558. After it come New Sharon (1,262), Eddyville (970) and Fremont (708), plus small communities such as Beacon and University Park. The population has hardly changed since 1980, so ownership here is stable and houses tend to change hands slowly.

Winters and summers both test an older house. A buyer's inspector will look first at the roof, furnace and gutters, which is worth remembering if you are deciding whether to fix things before you list. Old mining ground in the county also means some rural parcels have long paper trails, and deeds and parcel records are kept at the courthouse.

The Assessor and the Treasurer both work from the Mahaska County Courthouse, 106 South 1st Street, Oskaloosa. The Assessor decides value. The Treasurer collects the tax.

OfficePhoneHours
Assessor(641) 673-58058:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday
Treasurer (property tax)(641) 673-54828:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday

The Assessor page has Beacon maps and records, a sales report, and a Data Correction Form you can open from any parcel report. If your house has a new addition or lost a building, email the office with the address and a phone number.

Look up your parcel in Beacon first. Then you can ask the Assessor for an informal review between April 2 and April 25, or file a written protest by April 30. Those dates come from state law, Iowa Code 441.37, and the Department of Revenue.

A written protest goes on the state form and is signed by the owner or an agent. A board may allow electronic filing. Owners can also correct clerical or mathematical errors going back to earlier years, if those years are not fully paid.

  • Aim at the January 1 value, since that is the date assessments reflect.
  • If you argue the value is too high, bring recent sales nearby.
  • If you say the house is in the wrong class, bring proof of how it is used.

The local board of review hears protests starting May 1 and has until May 31 to finish. The state can grant an extension, but not past July 15. A written decision must be mailed within three days after adjournment.

An owner who still disagrees can go to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court. The deadline is 20 days from adjournment or May 31, whichever is later. Board members serve six-year staggered terms, and at least one must be a farmer (see the Iowa Department of Revenue summary).

The first half goes delinquent October 1 and the second half April 1, under Iowa Code chapter 445. A late half picks up interest of one and one-half percent for each month or part of a month.

Interest is rounded to the nearest whole dollar, with a $1 floor. Pay online through the Iowa Treasurers' parcel search, in person at the courthouse, or by mail to 106 S 1st Street. Before a closing, call the Treasurer at (641) 673-5482 for the exact amounts on your parcel.

Iowa treasurers offer delinquent parcels each June, normally on the third Monday, and the winning buyer pays the taxes, interest, fees and costs. The owner can redeem later by paying the sale price, a certificate fee and 2% interest per month (Iowa Code 446.7 and 447.1).

If you inherited a house with back taxes, check the parcel with the Treasurer first. Learning the balance before the sale is far better than learning it from a notice afterward.

sections.h2: Taxes and filings when you sell
sections.html:
Transfer tax is 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500 of value. A declaration of value goes in with the deed, and the recorder sends it to the assessor, who keeps it for three years (Iowa Code 428A.1).

The homestead credit affects the closing date. If the house sells before July 1, the new owner has to claim the credit by July 1. A sale on or after July 1 leaves the credit with the property for that year (rule 701-110.1).

  • Taxes are a lien on the parcel against everyone except the state.
  • A refund claim for tax paid in error must be made within two years of the due date.
  • The treasurer's receipt showing full payment is conclusive proof the parcel was free of taxes.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed, step by step
sections.html:
Start with the Treasurer at (641) 673-5482 and ask what is owed on the parcel, interest included. Then open the parcel report in Beacon and read it for mistakes in size, class or buildings. If you spot one, use the Data Correction Form, and in April consider a protest.

Next, decide how to sell. A traditional listing means preparing the house, waiting for a financed buyer and often handling repair requests. A cash sale as-is skips most of that. In either case the unpaid tax comes out of the price at closing, so the buyer gets the parcel free of it, and the treasurer's receipt is your proof. Ask the closing agent to confirm the payoff figure a few days ahead, because interest keeps adding up each month.

Gather three things first: a payoff statement, the parcel record and any repair or damage list. With those you can compare what you owe against what the house can sell for.

  • Pull the Beacon parcel report and use the Data Correction Form for wrong details.
  • Call the Treasurer for the current amount, interest included.
  • If the house is an inheritance, confirm which owners are of record at the courthouse.
  • Check whether the Assessor has a homestead credit on file, and tell the buyer.

If the numbers show more owed than you expected, or the repair list is long, a cash buyer who takes the house as-is can pay the taxes at closing and spare you the repairs. Compare that against a listing before you decide.

faqs.q: Where is the Mahaska County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: On the first floor of the Mahaska County Courthouse, 106 South 1st Street, Oskaloosa, IA 52577, in the southeast corner. Call (641) 673-5805, weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: What is the property tax protest window in Mahaska County?
faqs.a: April 2 through April 30, set by state law. An informal review with the Assessor runs April 2 through April 25.

faqs.q: How can I pay Mahaska County property tax?
faqs.a: Online through the Iowa Treasurers' parcel search, in person at the courthouse on weekdays, or by mail to 106 S 1st Street. The property tax line is (641) 673-5482.

faqs.q: How much is the late fee on Iowa property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is one and one-half percent per month, rounded to the nearest dollar, with a $1 minimum. A partial month counts as a full month.

faqs.q: Is Oskaloosa the biggest city in Mahaska County?
faqs.a: Yes. Oskaloosa had 11,558 residents in 2020 and is the county seat.
